summary: Temporary 60-ft wooden tower on Airfield Hill, Edgartown MA, built 1944 on state land and removed in 1946 on Navy order; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1946 by order of the US Navy; no source we read describes the Airfield Hill site today

events.note: Temporary 60-foot wooden tower built on state-owned land in Edgartown
Removed by order of the US Navy because it was a hazard to naval aviation
Present Vineyard Fire Tower built in 1950 in West Tisbury, a different site; the Register says the temporary tower near Edgartown was in service until then

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Fire Edgartown page says the Navy had the tower removed in 1946; the Register's Vineyard Fire Tower page says a temporary tower near Edgartown was in service until the 1950 tower was built. The story follows the 1946 removal order, which is specific, and reports the Register's account.

sources.title: Secret History of Martha's Vineyard During World War II

notes_for_editor: Record fields (county Dukes, elevation 32 m, kind tower, status gone) check out against the Forest Fire page; no correction. The Vineyard Gazette piece is context for the 1944-1946 Navy lease only; it does not say the lookout stood on the leased land, and the story does not claim that. The Naval Auxiliary Air Station wiki returned 403 and the Katama Airpark wiki covers a different airfield, so neither is used. No staffing, fire or access information in the sources read.
